body: It works when you use CONNECT_DEFERRED.

> It works when you use CONNECT_DEFERRED.

It is true that the **end result** works when using CONNECT_DEFERRED on the signal that changes the value (`_on_spinbox_focus_lost()` on the MRP). 

One little thing I noticed though when using this method is that the `value_changed` signal was being emmited twice when setting via property `value` and once when setting with `set_value_no_signal()`.

Steps to reproduce with the MRP:

1. Add the flag CONNECT_DEFERRED to the focus_exited signal so that it reads `spin_box.get_line_edit().focus_exited.connect(_on_spinbox_focus_lost, CONNECT_DEFERRED)`
2. Run the project and change the spinbox textbox to any number but 1 (Assume it's changed to 5).
3. Click on the line edit so the spinbox's textbox loses focus
4. Signal value_changed gets emmited saying the value changed to 5 even though we want it to be set to 1 (because of the counter) and we're using `set_value_no_signal()`.

After this the spinbox then gets set to 1 without emmiting the `value_changed` signal. On a different test, when setting the value directly by changing the variable `set_no_signal` to false (on the TestScene scene script) the `value_changed` signal is emmited twice. Assuming the same steps as above are done:

`value_changed` is emmited with the new value being 5, then
`value_changed` is emmited again with the new value being 1

Issue being that one expects the `value_changed` signal being emmited once when setting via `value` or none when setting with `set_value_no_signal()`.

Then again, I don't know if this is the intended behaviour.
